• Under PM-KISAN, eligible farmers receive ₹6,000 annually in three equal installments.

Further Insight:

• Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-KISAN)

• Launch Date: December 1, 2018

• Aim: Provide income support to small and marginal farmers.

• Main Features:

○ Direct cash transfer of ₹6,000 per year to eligible farmers, in three equal installments.

○ Covers approximately 14 crore farmers.

○ Focuses on financial inclusion and support to enhance agricultural productivity.

• PM Garib Kalyan Yojana (PMGKY) provided free food grains, direct cash transfers, and insurance coverage, but interest-free loans to traders were not part of it.

Further Insight:

• PM Garib Kalyan Yojana (PMGKY)

• Launch Date: December 16, 2016

• Aim: Provide welfare measures to the underprivileged, particularly during crises like COVID-19.

• Main Features:

○ Free food grains distribution, cash transfers to women, and insurance for healthcare workers.

○ Financial support for migrant workers.

○ Additional allocation for the MGNREGA employment guarantee scheme.

• The age limit for enrollment in the PM Shram Yogi Maan-Dhan (PM-SYM) pension scheme is between 18 and 40 years, and subscribers receive a pension after turning 60.

Further Insight:

• PM Shram Yogi Maan-Dhan (PM-SYM)

• Launch Date: February 15, 2019

• Aim: Provide pension benefits to workers in the unorganized sector.

• Main Features:

○ Voluntary and contributory pension scheme with a guaranteed pension of ₹3,000 per month after the age of 60.

○ Covers workers aged 18 to 40 years.

○ Joint contribution by the beneficiary and the government.

• One of the main goals of the Jal Shakti Ministry is to provide piped water supply (Har Ghar Jal) to all households by 2024.

Further Insight:

• Jal Shakti Ministry

• Launch Date: July 2019

• Aim: Ensure clean water access to all households and manage water resources efficiently.

• Main Features:

○ Integrates various water-related ministries and departments.

○ Focuses on the Jal Jeevan Mission (Har Ghar Jal) to provide piped drinking water to all rural households by 2024.

○ Supports initiatives like river rejuvenation, rainwater harvesting, and groundwater management.

• Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY) offers zero-balance accounts, insurance, and overdraft facilities, but it does not provide loans for small businesses.

Further Insight:

• Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY)

• Launch Date: August 28, 2014

• Aim: Promote financial inclusion by ensuring access to banking services for all citizens.

• Main Features:

○ Zero-balance savings accounts, overdraft facility, and RuPay debit cards.

○ Provides accidental insurance cover of ₹2 lakh.

○ Over 40 crore bank accounts have been opened under the scheme.

• The Skill India Mission aims to provide skill development and vocational training to create a globally competitive workforce.

Further Insight:

• Skill India Mission

• Launch Date: July 15, 2015

• Aim: Train and equip India's workforce with the necessary skills for employment and entrepreneurship.

• Main Features:

○ Focus on skill development in sectors like manufacturing, IT, and services.

○ Includes initiatives like PMKVY (Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana).

○ Aims to train over 40 crore people by 2022.

• Make in India initially focused on sectors like automobiles, pharmaceuticals, and tourism.

• Space exploration was not a key focus at the time.

Further Insight:

• Make in India

• Launch Date: September 25, 2014

• Aim: Promote manufacturing in India and attract foreign investment.

• Main Features:

○ Identifies 25 key sectors, including automobiles, electronics, tourism and pharmaceuticals.

○ Aims to increase the share of the manufacturing sector in GDP to 25% by 2025.

○ Provides incentives to boost innovation, R&D, and infrastructure development.

• The goal of Swachh Bharat Mission was to achieve a clean India by 2019, coinciding with Mahatma Gandhi's 150th birth anniversary.

Further Insight:

• Swachh Bharat Mission

• Launch Date: October 2, 2014

• Aim: Achieve a clean India by promoting sanitation and ending open defecation.

• Main Features:

○ Aimed at achieving the vision of "Clean India" by October 2, 2019.

○ Focuses on constructing household toilets, public toilets, and waste management systems.

○ Urban and rural components managed by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs and the Ministry of Jal Shakti, respectively.

• The Sukanya Samriddhi Scheme allows the opening of a girl child's account until she is 10 years old.

Further Insight:

• Sukanya Samriddhi Scheme (Beti Bachao Beti Padhao)

• Launch Date: January 22, 2015

• Aim: Promote the welfare of the girl child through education and financial security.

• Main Features:

○ Savings scheme offering high interest rates, with tax benefits.

○ Can be opened by parents of a girl child below the age of 10.

○ Provides financial support for the education and marriage of the girl child.

• The HRIDAY Scheme (Heritage City Development and Augmentation Yojana) focuses on preserving and revitalizing heritage cities.

Further Insight:

• HRIDAY (Heritage City Development and Augmentation Yojana)

• Launch Date: January 21, 2015

• Aim: Preserve and rejuvenate the heritage cities of India.

• Main Features:

○ Focus on urban infrastructure improvement and heritage conservation.

○ Supports 12 identified heritage cities, including Varanasi, Ajmer, and Amritsar.

○ Promotes sustainable tourism and urban development.

• The Tarun category under PMMY offers loans of up to ₹10 lakh for micro and small enterprises.

• ₹50,000 is for the Shishu category.

Further Insight:

• PM Mudra Yojana (PMMY)

• Launch Date: April 8, 2015

• Aim: Provide loans to non-corporate, non-farm small/micro enterprises.

• Main Features:

○ Loans up to ₹10 lakh under three categories:

■ Shishu (up to ₹50,000)

■ Kishore (₹50,000 to ₹5 lakh)

■ Tarun (₹5 lakh to ₹10 lakh).

○ Focus on entrepreneurship development, particularly for small businesses.

○ Offers financial inclusion and employment generation opportunities.

• Ujala Yojana distributes energy-efficient 9-watt LED bulbs to households.

Further Insight:

• Ujala Yojana

• Launch Date: January 5, 2015

• Aim: Promote energy efficiency by distributing LED bulbs at affordable prices.

• Main Features:

○ Distributed over 36 crore LED bulbs, saving energy and reducing electricity bills.

○ Reduces carbon emissions and promotes energy conservation.

○ Supports the goal of sustainable development and environmental protection.

• The minimum pension under APY is ₹1,000 per month, depending on the contribution made by the subscriber.

Further Insight:

• Atal Pension Yojana (APY)

• Launch Date: May 9, 2015

• Aim: Provide a defined pension to all citizens, particularly those in the unorganized sector.

• Main Features:

○ Offers a guaranteed minimum pension of ₹1,000 to ₹5,000 per month after the age of 60.

○ Voluntary subscription with joint contribution by the subscriber and the government.

○ Focuses on old-age income security for low-income groups.

• The annual premium for life insurance coverage under PMJJBY is ₹330.

Further Insight:

• PM Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY)

• Launch Date: May 9, 2015

• Aim: Provide affordable life insurance coverage to citizens.

• Main Features:

○ Life insurance cover of ₹2 lakh for a premium of ₹330 per year.

○ Available to individuals aged 18 to 50 years.

○ Provides financial security to families in case of the insured's death.

• Under PMSBY, ₹1 lakh is provided for partial disability. Full disability or death results in a coverage of ₹2 lakh.

Further Insight:

• PM Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY)

• Launch Date: May 9, 2015

• Aim: Provide accidental death and disability coverage to citizens.

• Main Features:

○ Accidental death and disability cover of ₹2 lakh for a premium of ₹12 per year.

○ Available to individuals aged 18 to 70 years.

○ Covers both partial and total disabilities resulting from accidents.

• Atal Bhujal Yojana focuses on the sustainable management of groundwater resources in India.

Further Insight:

• Atal Bhujal Yojana (ABY)

• Launch Date: December 25, 2019

• Aim: Improve groundwater management in water-stressed areas.

• Main Features:

○ Focus on community-led sustainable management of groundwater resources.

○ Aimed at improving water conservation, enhancing groundwater recharge, and promoting sustainable water use.

○ Total outlay of ₹6,000 crore, with part funding from the World Bank.

• Digital India does not specifically offer free Wi-Fi for rural households. It focuses on digital infrastructure, governance, and literacy.

Further Insight:

• Digital India

• Launch Date: July 1, 2015

• Aim: Transform India into a digitally empowered society and knowledge economy.

• Main Features:

○ Focuses on creating digital infrastructure, providing e-governance services, and promoting digital literacy.

○ Includes programs like BharatNet, eKranti, and UMANG (Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance).

○ Aims to connect rural India with high-speed internet and promote financial inclusion through digital services.

• Minimum deposit required under the Gold Monetization Scheme to open gold saving account is 10 grams.

Further Insight:

• Gold Monetization Scheme (GMS)

• Launch Date: November 4, 2015

• Aim: Mobilize the gold held by households and institutions to put it to productive use.

• Main Features:

○ Allows individuals to deposit their gold in a GMS account and earn interest.

○ Minimum deposit required: 10 grams of raw gold (bars, coins, jewelry).

○ Helps reduce India's dependence on gold imports by encouraging domestic gold deposits.

• UDAY does not provide interest-free loans; it focuses on reducing DISCOM losses, improving efficiency, and issuing bonds to restructure debt.

• Reducing transmission losses is a goal.

• Issuing bonds is a key part of the scheme.

• Improving operational efficiency is one of its objectives.

Further Insight:

• Ujwal DISCOM Assurance Yojana (UDAY)

• Launch Date: November 2015

• Aim: Financial turnaround and operational improvement of state power distribution companies (DISCOMs).

• Main Features:

○ Focuses on reducing debt and improving the financial health of DISCOMs.

○ Encourages states to take over 75% of DISCOM debt and issue bonds.

○ Aims at reducing transmission losses and improving power distribution efficiency.

• The Stand-Up India scheme is designed to provide loans to SC/ST individuals and women entrepreneurs to promote entrepreneurship.

Further Insight:

• Stand-Up India

• Launch Date: April 5, 2016

• Aim: Promote entrepreneurship among women and SC/ST communities.

• Main Features:

○ Provides loans between ₹10 lakh and ₹1 crore for setting up greenfield enterprises.

○ Focus on empowering women and marginalized communities through entrepreneurship.

○ Supports enterprises in manufacturing, services, or trading sectors.
